title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens Section IV ('Explicit descriptions by Weierstrass ℘-functions'). Grothendieck sets up a coordinate-free framework for deriving the Weierstrass equation.

Setup: E is an elliptic curve over a field k of characteristic ≠ 2. For n ∈ ℕ put F_n = Γ(E, O(n·0_E)), the functions with a pole of order at most n at the origin.

By Riemann–Roch, dim F_n = n for n ≥ 1, and F_0 = F_1 = k·1. The union F_∞ = lim F_n = Γ(E − {0}, O) is the affine coordinate ring. Multiplication satisfies F_m·F_n ⊂ F_{m+n}. So F_* = ⊕ F_n is a graded algebra: the Rees algebra of the pole-order filtration, which is also the section ring of the ample sheaf O(0_E). Its Proj is canonically E.

The aim is to determine F_* explicitly. It is generated by 1 ∈ F_1, x ∈ F_2 and y ∈ F_3, giving E as a cubic in the weighted projective plane P(1,2,3).

The key tool is the exact sequence 0 → F_{n-1} → F_n → t_E^{⊗n} → 0 for n ≥ 2. Here t_E = T_{E,0} is the tangent space at the origin. The map ε_n takes the leading polar coefficient: O(nP)/O((n−1)P) restricted to P is canonically T_P^{⊗n}.

The page ends by introducing, for δ ∈ t_E, an operation. On the next page this is the invariant derivation θ_δ : F_n → F_{n+1}, compatible with these sequences. That shows ker θ_δ = constants, followed by the involution f ↦ f(−x).

The point of the construction is to keep track of the canonical t_E-twists. Weierstrass coefficients then become sections of powers of t_E (i.e. of ω^{⊗-k}), which is what one needs for a version over the moduli stack and for the link with modular forms.
errors: None substantive. The exact sequence (6) is correctly restricted to n ≥ 2: for n = 1 the map to t_E is zero, since F_0 = F_1.
The symbol ∐ for the graded algebra means a direct sum. This is Grothendieck's usual notation, not an error.

ideas.what: Filtration of functions by pole order at the origin, and the associated graded/Rees algebra whose Proj recovers E
ideas.modern_name: Section ring of O(0_E) / Rees algebra; Weierstrass model in P(1,2,3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass); the scheme-theoretic form is in Deligne's 'Courbes elliptiques: formulaire' (1975) and Katz–Mazur

ideas.what: Canonical identification of the graded pieces F_n/F_{n-1} with t_E^{⊗n} via leading polar coefficients
ideas.modern_name: Coordinate-free Weierstrass theory; weights given by powers of ω^{-1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, Katz (modular forms as sections of ω^{⊗k})
ideas.where_published: Deligne, Formulaire; Katz, p-adic properties of modular schemes and modular forms (1973)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, intrinsic set-up of the standard Riemann–Roch derivation of the Weierstrass equation. It is well documented in Deligne's and Katz's work from the 1970s, with nothing new on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the phrase after 'sur corps' (with a crossed-out word) is not reliably 'des pˢ communs'. It is likely 'sur corps k' plus a parenthetical about the field. It is uncertain, but mathematically just 'over a field k'.
'On a une sur (4)' should read 'On a sur F_∞ := lim F_n une loi de multiplication ass. comm.' (associative commutative multiplication on F_∞).
(6): the arrow label is ε_n, and the target is t_E^{⊗n}.
